title: Minimax Detection of Signed Carryover Tails under Independent versus Blocked Switchback Assignment
banked_reason: D0.5.G below field floor: subfield, paper_score_ceiling 7.0<7.4, salvageable=false; independent validity gate confirms terminal below-floor. Math and positioning panel receipts remain revise; archive is not a panel-passed or Lean-verified theorem package.
gap_reasons: The delivered contribution is confined to a constant-baseline FIR experiment with known unit Gaussian noise and observed randomized prehistory; robustness to baseline drift, unknown noise structure, and broader operational carryover models is not established. Within this benchmark, the fixed-direction information argument and integrated-score calibration establish the advertised full-range rates with original-likelihood all-test converses, so the unresolved empirical-information question is not load-bearing and the TL;DR contains no stale frontier claim. The cited [FIR concentration theorem](https://arxiv.org/html/1911.12794v1) retains a logarithmic horizon restriction and does not supply the proportional-horizon result verbatim. The explicit upper constants, especially the integer-Gram finite branch, provide no useful numerical planning guarantee, while the delivered computations do not evaluate the attaining integrated-score tests' power against signed and gapped tails. These scope and practical-calibration limitations constrain the projected paper score to 7.0 and leave the result below a broadly consequential framework or flagship resolution. tldr: In a one-unit constant-baseline Gaussian FIR benchmark with observed randomized prehistory, the full-record minimax separation is \(H^{1/4}/\sqrt T\) under independent period assignments and \(H/\sqrt T\) under observed-phase two-period blocking throughout \(T\ge64\), \(1\le H\le\lfloor T/8\rfloor\). Total full-record tests attain both rates, the original joint likelihood supplies matching all-test converses, and the blocking penalty is \(H^{3/4}\). The normalized empirical inverse-square quantiles remain open but are unnecessary for the frontier.
gap: Scalar carryover projections leave gaps and cancellation unresolved. Existing overlapping-input concentration restricts the lag horizon, while known-information inverse-testing theory omits the primitive randomization step.
